guidelines_reference.diabetes: American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care
guidelines_reference.cardiovascular: American Heart Association (AHA) Lifestyle & Sodium Guidelines
guidelines_reference.kidney: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Clinical Practice Guidelines

carbohydrate_guidance.rationale: ADA recommends individualized carbohydrate intake emphasizing fiber-rich whole grains, non-starchy vegetables, and lean proteins rather than rigid elimination.

purine_scoring.rationale: Purine management requires balancing portion and frequency alongside adequate hydration, rather than a universal hard threshold.

sodium_guidelines.rationale: AHA recommends working toward an ideal sodium target of ≤1,500 mg/day where clinically appropriate, with a general upper limit of 2,300 mg/day.

ckd_kidney_disease.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
ckd_kidney_disease.rationale: KDIGO guidelines mandate individualized medical nutrition therapy for CKD based on stage, eGFR, electrolyte levels, and dialysis status. Automated high-protein or severe electrolyte restrictions require clinical supervision.

goitrogen_policy.rationale: Thorough cooking substantially deactivates myrosinase and reduces goitrogenic activity. Normal cooked portions of cruciferous vegetables with adequate iodine are safe and nutritious.

pregnancy_lactation.name: Pregnancy & Lactation
pregnancy_lactation.rationale: Aggressive caloric deficits or restrictive ketogenic protocols during pregnancy and active breastfeeding can compromise fetal growth or milk supply.

SAFE.description: Generally compatible with the user's active diet, metabolic goals, and medical profile.

CAUTION.description: Suitable for consumption with mindful attention to portion size, preparation method, or meal balance.

LIMIT.description: Consumable in moderation; large portions or high frequency are not recommended for this condition/diet.

AVOID.description: Incompatible with the user's verified food allergies or strict clinical contraindications.

PROFESSIONAL_REVIEW.description: NutriLens cannot safely determine suitability automatically. Personalized evaluation by a qualified healthcare professional is recommended.
